Every tie's every source was re-read at assembly; no script rebuilds this file.
notes: The travel (AAU) basketball clubs that players on the 58 boys basketball rosters MaxPreps lists so far are tied to. The linking rule is field hockey's (README, "Clubs"): a public page must name the player and a basketball club or program, and either name the player's high school (with the right city where a school of the name exists elsewhere), or give the roster's class year with a hometown in the school's own area. A name alone never counts, a class year that disagrees with the roster rules a match out (except one a year ahead of a roster grade that is last season's: see data/basketball/rosters-enrichment.json), and social media is never a source.

Club records (13): written from each club's own site, or the adidas 3SSB program directory, for the clubs our players' pages name, the programs the circuits list near the schools, and those met on the way. No public directory lists the boys' travel programs of any area (the Nike EYBL team list is an image, Puma's and others are drawn by script or refuse automated reads), so no area was searched for every club: the Peninsula and the South Bay most, San Francisco, the East Bay and Marin only for clubs a player's page names. No club based in Santa Cruz County was found. No record names a coach.

Ties: 50 for 47 players at 27 schools. Sources: Prep Hoops player pages ("attends <school> ... and plays club basketball for <club>", the school linked to its Prep Hoops team page, whose title gives the city) and the evaluation cards in its articles; Hudl profiles' team lists (on the school's own team); NCSA profiles' dated Club Information lines; SportsRecruits profiles' club block (read twice through the page's JSON); MaxPreps career pages' club-teams block. Club names are mapped to a record by hand: Esface to Team Esface; SV Soldiers to Silicon Valley Soldiers; Bay City Warriors to Bay City Basketball (its high school boys' program, by the club's own site); Oakland Soldiers E16 EYBL to Oakland Soldiers; San Jose Spartans 300 Elite to San Jose Spartans; NBBA to North Bay Basketball Academy; Hudl's 'Gold Basketball' to Peninsula Gold; HoopRight and Hoop Right to HoopRight; Oakland Soldiers Navy (an NCSA team label) to Oakland Soldiers.

Status. current: a source dated 2026 (a Prep Hoops article's 2026 session roster naming the club team, a Hudl entry reaching 2026, an NCSA Club Information line for 2026, a MaxPreps entry joined or edited in 2026). past: a Hudl entry ending in 2024 or earlier, an older NCSA line when a newer one names another club, or a MaxPreps entry last edited before 2025. unknown: everything else, including every Prep Hoops player page (undated; the date shown is the profile's creation). Where sources differ, current is shown before unknown, and unknown before past.

Left out: Serra players' Prep Hoops pages, which say 'Junipero Serra-San Mateo' but link the Gardena school's team page (not the right school); pages giving a school with no city where a namesake exists (a St. Ignatius card with no city; a Willow Glen page placed in Nevada); a Hudl 'AmFb Combine' entry (an event in Lincoln, NE, not a club); club entries for teams before sixth grade; JV players' ties (jvAffiliations is empty).

No record, so no tie shown, although a page ties a rostered player to the club: Team California (2), Seattle Rotary (2), Roadrunners Sports Club (2), Seattle Rotary (EYBL) (2), All In Elite (5), South Bay Snipers (1), San Jose Ninjas (1), Team elite (1), Team Evolution (1), Bay Area Sonics (1), RBA Waves (1), Flight Academy (2), Santa Cruz Premier (2), Silicon Valley Basketball Club (2), Wce Silicon Valley 14ua (1), Fierce (1), All In (2), AYB 14u-Liu (2), Top Flight Elite (2), South Bay Reapers (1), HoopSphere Academy (1), Genesis Basketball (1), Prodigy (1), Work Hard Play Hard (1), AAU Bulldawgs (1), Roadrunners (1), RBA waves (2), Wolfpack Elite (1), Bay Area impact (2), BAAS Dragons (1), San Francisco Cyclones (1), Evolution Adidas Gold (1), WCE East Bay (1), Bay Area Rebels (1). No club-owned site or circuit directory entry was found for these (All In Elite, Team California, Seattle Rotary and Roadrunners Sports Club are named on Prep Hoops pages; the rest on MaxPreps career pages or NCSA Club Information lines; an NCSA line's KOPA entries were left out as unclear).

Every source of every tie was re-read at assembly on 2026-11-21 by a separate script and its quote found on the page as served (Hudl and MaxPreps: the page's own data fields; SportsRecruits: the profile JSON, twice; NCSA: the page re-read once more).

No record, so their matches are not linked: South Bay Snipers (Passport record: San Jose, no website. southbaysnipers.com exists but is a GoDaddy "Launching Soon" page with no club content; only a Lessons.com trainer listing found.); Wolfpack Zeta (Passport record: Sunnyvale, no website. No program of this name found; wolfpackbasketball.org is a Culver City (LA) club, and a "Wolfpack Basketball Norcal" is Tri-Valley. Likely a team name; no club site.); All-In-Elite (Passport record says Rocklin (Sacramento area) with website Allinyouthsports.com, which redirects to an unrelated trainer (EA Sports Development); allinelite.org is a "coming soon" placeholder. No own site, and its city does not fit the San Jose players.); Pacifica Basketball Club (Passport record: Pacifica (401 Paloma Ave, the Oceana High School address), no website; no site found (guessed hosts do not resolve; search found nothing).); No Limit Basketball (Passport record gives only state WA, no website. nolimitbasketball.com is an Illinois club (tryouts at Dwight Township Fieldhouse), not ours; no Bay Area site found.); Fierce Basketball (fiercebasketball.com (SportsEngine) is a youth training program (private workouts, small groups, clinics) with a 408 phone, but neither it nor the Passport record (state CA only) names a city, and it lists no teams.); South Bay Reapers (Passport record: Gilroy, no website; no site found.); Cali Legends (Passport record: Seaside, no website (social media only); no site found.); Salinas Valley Kings (Passport record: Gonzales, no website (social media only); no site found.); NBC BULLS 2028 (Passport record: San Jose, no website; appears to be a single class-of-2028 team; no site found.); SF Work Hard Play Hard (Passport record: San Francisco 94134, website whphbasketball.com, which does not resolve (DNS failure); no other own site found.); Bay Area Lakers (Passport record: San Jose 95133, website field is an Instagram handle ("https://@BAL322433"); no site found.); Team California (The Passport public program endpoint answers 404 "Program not found" for 14250; no Bay Area club site of this name found.); MVP Magic (Passport record: Oakland 94705, no website; only a G365 event report names it; no site found.); MBA Triple Threat (Passport record: Gilroy, no website (social media only); Triple Threat Academy (Oakland/Alameda/San Ramon) is a different program; no site found.).

League rosters, 2026-11-27 (README, "Club rosters in the other sports"): the boys club team rosters of the Northern California events on The Passport (G365, The Stage, Breakthrough, Strictly Hoops, For the Love of the Game, the adidas 3Stripes Gold West Regional) and the adidas 3SSB sessions, read from its public API into data/basketball/club-rosters.json (pnpm fetch-club-rosters:basketball: 667 teams, 5,685 players with class years), compared with every varsity and JV row by pnpm compare-club-rosters:basketball. For every row the league-roster rule matched (and the rows it left only for a club with no record, two clubs, or a club away from the schools), each player's own Passport record (players/by-player-number/<n>) and team history were read: a record naming the row's school makes the tie high (rule (a), the player's own record); one naming no school needs a hometown in the school's county or one bordering it (rule (b)) and is medium; one naming another high school, or a hometown farther away, rules the match out (Cupertino's Michael Wong is a Dougherty Valley player; Hollister's Derrick Jones an Overfelt one; Milpitas' Deren Cayabyab lives in Elk Grove; three SHC, SI and King's Academy names live in Oakland, Hayward, Richmond and Antioch), and a record giving no hometown links nothing (7 rows). 101 new ties (25 high, 76 medium) and 11 that other pages had made, which gain the roster; ten club records added for them (above). Not linked: 10 rows on two programs' rosters in one season, and about 80 at programs with no record.

2026-11-27, the owner's decision: the area a club may be based in for a league roster to link (rule 5, LOCAL_REGIONS) is the whole Bay Area (San Francisco, the Peninsula, the South Bay, the East Bay and Marin) and the Central Coast, in every sport. Under it St. Ignatius' Noah Kirsch-Lopez and Huck Lemmer link to Lakeshow (East Bay): each player's own Passport record gives the class of 2028 and a San Francisco hometown and lists the Lakeshow team (medium). On a second decision the same day the hometown test on the player's own record (for a record that names no school) was widened to the same area: a hometown in the Bay Area (San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda, Contra Costa and Marin counties) or on the Central Coast (Santa Cruz, Monterey, San Benito), where it had been the school's county or one bordering it. It changed one tie: St. Ignatius' Anthony Otis (hometown Richmond), whose Bay City tie gains its 17U 3SGB roster and reads current. The other players it had kept out are at programs with no record here (Team California, NBC Bulls 2028, SDS Unlimited, Evolve Performance, Flight Academy, King Academy) or on two programs' rosters; Milpitas' Deren Cayabyab (Elk Grove) stays out.

2026-11-27, the owner's decision: a program with no site of its own may take The Passport's public program record (api.the-passport.com/api/programs/public/<n>: a CLUB, with its city; its director and contact fields are not recorded) as its club record. Nine of the programs note 7 lists as having no record now have one: South Bay Snipers (San Jose), Pacifica Basketball Club (Pacifica), South Bay Reapers (Gilroy), Cali Legends (Seaside), Salinas Valley Kings (Gonzales), NBC Bulls (San Jose; The Passport's NBC BULLS 2028), SF Work Hard Play Hard (San Francisco; its listed website whphbasketball.com does not resolve), MVP Magic (Oakland) and MBA Triple Threat (Gilroy), each with its teams at the events of data/basketball/club-rosters.json. Their matches, under the same tests on each player's own Passport record (note 8, widened in note 9), made 40 ties (14 high, 26 medium), every roster and record re-read the same day. Still no record: Wolfpack Zeta, All-In-Elite, No Limit Basketball, Fierce Basketball, Bay Area Lakers and Team California (note 7). The page ties note 5 lists for South Bay Snipers, South Bay Reapers and Work Hard Play Hard were not re-made.

Other forms of a name, 2026-11-28 (owner decision: tie a player a club roster lists under another form of the name, when everything else agrees; a class year one off is accepted when the player is very likely the same). The league-roster rule was run with each row's first name in its other forms (isAnotherFormOf in lib/players/club-rosters.ts), each roster source names the roster's spelling in `rosterName`, and each player's own Passport record was read as for the other ties: Ani Menon (Monta Vista, HoopRight, Anirudh), Ben Camhi (Westmont, South Bay H2G, Benjamin), Ranvi Sinha (Leland, South Bay Snipers, Ranvijay), Nick Gklaros-Stavropoulos (Mitty, Team Lillard, Nicky), Grant Coblin (St. Ignatius, Bay City, Grantham) and Ben Wu (Pinewood, Bay Area Impact, Benjamin), medium on a Bay Area hometown; Tim Ofa (Lincoln, South Bay H2G, Timote), high, his record naming Lincoln High School; Max Grudin (Priory, as Maxwell), high, his record naming Woodside Priory, to Lakeshow (15U 3SSB, July 2026, current) and DM's Mavericks (16U, May 2026, unknown), his class year (2028, as his Hudl page says) the grade above MaxPreps' stale one, which the roster overlay already marks rosterBehind. Left out: Eli Hernandez (Live Oak JV), whose Passport record names Ann Sobrato High School. Every roster and record was read live the same day.

Club records added 2026-11-28 (the owner asked for records for clubs without one, where it makes sense): for the programs whose rosters list a tracked player the league-roster rule had left only for want of a record, each player's own Passport record was read first, and a program got a record only where a tie would follow. Evolve Performance (Oakland), Flight Academy Basketball (Daly City), SDS Unlimited (Fremont), Ronin (San Jose), F.O.A (Salinas) and East Bay Athletics (Oakland) have no site of their own (searched the same day), so their Passport program records are their club records (owner decision 2026-11-27); Top Flight Elite Basketball's is written from its own site (topflightelite.com, Campbell).
